text: The evening light lay gold across the bush.
Sunny wandered underneath the tallest trees.
High on a branch she saw a flash of white,
and a yellow crest that rose up like a crown.
A cockatoo, as white as morning clouds,
was getting ready for his beauty sleep.
He preened each snowy feather into place,
as careful as a king before his rest.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “You look very smart.”
“One must look tidy for one's dreams,” he said.
He raised his yellow crest to say goodnight,
a little golden sunrise in the dusk.
“All day I call and fly and play,” he said,
“but when the light goes soft, I settle down.”
So Sunny settled too, upon the grass,
and watched the last gold fade between the leaves.
The cockatoo grew quiet on his branch,
his white wings folded neat against the night.
He tucked his head beneath his snowy wing,
a little cloud asleep up in the tree.
Sunny found a bed of fallen leaves,
and curled up underneath the sleeping cloud.
The bush was still. The moon rose white and round.
Everything was peaceful, calm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy in the silver light.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath her snowy friend,
both of them as peaceful as the moon.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, white cockatoo.
Goodnight, sleepy trees. Goodnight, little one.
